result.title: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward"
result.summary: Reinforcement learning has achieved strong performance in many tasks by letting agents learn from nothing more than a reward signal. However, in more complex tasks, agents still struggle to learn good, generalizable policies, even with carefully designed rewards and abundant samples. We argue that this difficulty stems from the reward decoding burden: designers encode their knowledge of the desired behavior into rewards and penalties, and agents must infer this knowledge from long sequences of noisy scalars. To address this burden, we propose prescriptive policy learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents higher-level knowledge about the tasks, termed principles of behavior, such as how to maintain balance, how to accumulate energy, and how to land smoothly. Through appropriately selected key quantities and references, PPL can directly indicate at every step whether the agent follows the principles and to what extent. Our experiments show that agents can learn good, generalizable policies without any reward. Taught only simple heuristic principles, PPL agents outperform reward-based methods with far fewer samples. Their policies also transfer directly to harder settings and keep performing well, demonstrating their strong generalization ability. In summary, PPL provides a new approach in which rough knowledge of the desired behavior is enough for agents to learn good, generalizable policies, even when the system dynamics cannot be accurately modeled.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 prescriptive policy learning（PPL）：用设计者给定的「行为原则」替代奖励信号，通过选取关键量与参考值，在每一步直接判断智能体是否遵循原则及遵循程度，从而在无奖励条件下学到样本效率更高、可迁移的策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其逐步原则符合度信号本质上是由先验知识构造的密集过程监督，可能为 LVR 中中间推理步骤的贡献分配与监督设计提供线索；但论文属 RL 控制任务，无视觉或 latent 状态研究，需核查迁移可行性。
